trust_decision.summary: Genuine pre-fix upstream code: the pinned tree allocates an APEv2 tag-item value from the attacker-declared size with no bound, and the published commit only adds guards plus a chunked reader, so the vulnerability is real and removed by the diff rather than planted.

landing_point.why: The summary names the APEv2 parser and 'memory allocation'; the first thing an engineer sees is `const picData = new Uint8Array(tagItemHeader.size)` in the cover-art (binary) branch, fed straight from the 32-bit item header.

fix_sites.entry_point: APEv2Parser.parseTags (via parseBuffer / parseFile / parseStream / parseBlob / parseWebStream / parseFromTokenizer)
APEv2Parser.readTagValue, called from the text_utf8 and binary item branches

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The fallback buffer is sized by the caller-declared file size rather than by a tag-item field, so a solver can argue it is a different allocation from the advisory's item-size sink and was never covered by the published fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate item values larger than one 64 KiB chunk must still come back intact - a real 48,658-byte embedded cover, NUL-separated multi-value text, and the skipCovers option which must still skip artwork without buffering it.

O6_input_shapes: item size larger than the tag's own remaining byte budget (footer.size bookkeeping)
item size larger than the remaining file bytes
key with no NUL terminator inside the tag boundary (peek window must not run into the value)
non-random-access tokenizer with unknown file size
non-random-access tokenizer with an advertised file size larger than the actual stream (truncated input)
all four dataType values combined with skipCovers true and false
values above 64 KiB that need several chunk reads before assembly

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Non-random-access tokenizer with a declared but untrustworthy file size: when the 32-byte footer probe at the current position is not 'APETAGEX', the whole remaining declared size is allocated in one `new Uint8Array(remaining)` before any payload byte is read; the published fix never touches this allocation.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a whole-tag fallback buffer, not a tag-item value, and its size comes from the caller's fileInfo.size, so it can be argued to be outside the advisory's item-size protection.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different method (tryParseApeHeader) about 35 lines above the fixed loop; reached from the APE, WavPack and Musepack routes

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Read a WavPack metadata sub-block of declared size into `new Uint8Array(dataSizeInWords * 2 - ...)` with no bound against the remaining block or file.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: WavPack files carry APEv2 tags and this parser already hands over to the APEv2 parser, so a maintainer hardening the APE tag path plausibly writes the same declared-size read for the sibling container in the same commit series.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second declared-size allocation (the whole remaining tag/file) living beside the item-value reader.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already exists in the pinned file as the appending-header fallback; writing it the same way as the new chunked reader is the natural symmetrical change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A copy of the chunked streaming read that a new container reader could reach for, or deliberately omit.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the exact compliant twin of the new readTagValue helper, added by the immediately preceding in-tree fix, so a maintainer adding a fourth reader would copy it - and a planted sibling could be the same code with the random-access condition dropped.

O9_family: resource exhaustion: uncontrolled memory allocation from an attacker-declared length (CWE-789)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js >= 18, yarn 4, tsc (lib/tsconfig.json), mocha + chai, biome for lint
O10_build.project_tests: test/test-file-ape.ts (APE plus APEv2-in-MP3 issue #331) driven through the parseFile / parseStream / parseWebStream / parseBlob matrix in test/metadata-parsers.ts, with test-file-wavpack.ts and test-file-musepack.ts covering the other routes; no length/allocation tests exist at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `if (size > fileInfo.size - position) throw` and keep `new Uint8Array(size)`, which passes the parseBuffer PoC but leaves streams with unknown size allocating the declared item size and leaves the unterminated-key underflow in place.

out_of_scope_notes: Same class of bug in another format parser, outside this APEv2 advisory: a WavPack metadata sub-block is allocated as `new Uint8Array(dataSizeInWords * 2 - ...)` straight from the block's own 1-3 byte length field (lib/wavpack/WavPackParser.ts:87).
unverified: Repo size in MB could not be measured (no shell in this session); tiny_repo is inferred from 13,580 lines of TypeScript across 97 files under lib/ plus the test tree, far below 5 MB of source.
Whether the uncovered route at lib/apev2/APEv2Parser.ts:111-116 is still present today: no latest release was supplied, so present_in_latest is unknown.
